summary: Keepalive/backoff misalignment + HTTP/2 multiplexing causing head-of-line blocking and perceived inference lag
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent multi-second slowdowns for generation requests from their service that appear as long tails (95-99th percentile spikes). These spikes correlate with a high number of client retries and a rise in 5xx/timeout retries logged at the API gateway.

Impact:
- Customer-facing chat experiences show delayed replies for ~15% of sessions during peak traffic windows, causing SLA alerts and user complaints.
- Revenue-impacting for ChatFlow’s paid tier (enterprise contracts).

Environment:
- Redwood hosted API (prod), region: us-east-1
- Customer SDK: redwood-js v1.11.2 (HTTP/2 enabled by default in their environment)
- Backend models used: rwdl-phi-2.1 and rwdl-psi-1.0 (mixed workload)

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Run steady stream of short prompt requests (avg tokens=30) at ~300 req/s using SDK default client configuration.
2) Observe 95p/99p latency spikes after ~20–40 minutes of sustained load.
3) If maxConnections is increased locally, spikes reduce.

Observed behavior / logs:
- Gateway logs show a pattern: burst of new request attempts, followed by rapid client-side retry storms (exponential backoff starting at 100ms, max cap 10s, no jitter).
- SDK metrics: socket churn increases (many short-lived TLS handshakes), concurrent in-flight requests exceed pool size, HTTP/2 stream queueing increases per connection.
- Serving runtime traces show normal token generation latency once request reaches rack; delays are pre-rack (transport/queueing).

Initial hypothesis:
- Combination of aggressive deterministic backoff (no randomized jitter) and conservative HTTP connection pool sizing leads to head-of-line blocking. With HTTP/2 multiplexing, long-lived streams and socket churn reduce available streams on existing connections and new requests queue behind inflight/blocked streams. TLS session reuse disabled in the customer's infra increases handshake overhead and short-lived sockets.

Investigation notes:
- Reproduced locally by running redwood-js v1.11.2 with maxConnections=6 and backoff policy: fixed base 100ms, multiplier 2, no jitter. Observed identical 95p spikes after ~25 minutes.
- Turning on jitter and increasing pool to 40 eliminated the spikes in load test.
- Packet captures from customer (pcap) show many TLS handshakes and RSTs when pool is saturated.
- Related logs: API gateway trace IDs 20260310-ARK-0091 through ARK-0098 attached by customer.

Mitigation / workaround provided to customer:
- Immediate: bump SDK client maxConnections to 30 and enable HTTP keepalive with 90s idle timeout; enable randomized jitter (uniform or full jitter) in backoff. This reduced 99p from ~3.8s to ~420ms in customer staging.
- Short-term: recommend SDK upgrade to redwood-js v1.12.0 which defaults to jittered backoff and safe pool sizing heuristics.
- Long-term: SDK team will ship telemetry to detect "pool saturation patterns" and warn users when default config may cause head-of-line blocking.

Next steps / open action items:
- SDK: ship v1.12.3 patch to make jitter required and to change default maxConnections heuristic for HTTP/2 heavy clients. (assigned SDK-ENG).
- Customer Success: confirm customer applied recommended config to production (ChatFlow to confirm by 2026-03-16).
- Observability: add dashboard alert for "client retry ratio > 5% and new TLS handshakes per second > threshold".
